result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B says plainly that the typography is sound, lists what already works and makes three small, justified changes. It leaves the sizes, measure, leading and character of the page alone. A also opens with praise, but then makes eight changes, styles elements nobody asked about and switches the table to display: block, which costs accessibility. Its clamp(), antialiasing and lining-nums changes go past what a pre-launch second look needs. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A says plainly that the typography is sound and limits itself to two small, well-justified fixes (th alignment and table margin) plus one optional addition. It returns only the changed lines and leaves the measure, sizes and character of the page intact. B rewrites and expands the stylesheet, changes the h1 sizing and table display, and adds many elements and smoothing tweaks no one asked for. Some of B's points are valid, but most of it is padding the night before launch, and the display:block table hurts accessibility.
